transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. We've got the change request to retire the legacy CI runner image and move all repositories to the replacement image, with a proposed cutover date of June 21. The replacement image has already passed the standard build, integration, and security smoke tests as of today, June 14. Before I can approve this change, I need release engineering and security compliance to review the proposal and state any blockers or required controls. Let's start with release engineering -- do you have any concerns or blockers with disabling the legacy image on June 21?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a blocker. While handling a failed build this morning, I confirmed that the Atlas and Birch repositories still require a compiler that is only available in the legacy runner image. Their migration work will take exactly 10 business days. I haven't updated the change request yet because the migration estimate was only confirmed this morning. Disabling the legacy image on June 21 would break CI for those repositories.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a required control to surface. During a compliance evidence review yesterday, I confirmed that every production CI build using the replacement image must emit signed provenance records that are retained for exactly 365 days before the legacy image can be retired. I haven't filed the control update yet because the evidence review is still being reconciled, but this is a blocker for approving the June 21 cutover -- the provenance requirement must be in place and verified before we retire the legacy image.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for surfacing these. Let me make sure I have this right. Casey, you're saying Atlas and Birch repositories still depend on a compiler only available in the legacy runner image, and their migration will take exactly 10 business days -- so disabling the legacy image on June 21 would break CI for those repos. Morgan, you're saying every production CI build using the replacement image must emit signed provenance records retained for exactly 365 days, and this control must be in place and verified before we can retire the legacy image. Both of these are blockers for the June 21 cutover as proposed. I cannot approve the change request as written on that timeline. Here's what I'd like to do: keep the legacy runner image enabled in the production CI fleet for now, exclude Atlas and Birch from the mandatory cutover until their migration is complete, and require that the signed provenance control with 365-day retention be implemented and verified before we fully retire the legacy image. Casey, please update the change request with the Atlas and Birch migration details and a revised timeline. Morgan, please file the control update once your evidence review is reconciled so we can track it formally. Once both of those are done, we can set a revised cutover date that accounts for the 10-business-day migration and the provenance verification. Does that work for everyone?
